data.heading: People decide. Software does the legwork. Nothing moves without a name on it.
data.lede: We're marketers first. We built our own software because the tools we rented couldn't show us what was happening in an account every day. Here's how an engagement actually runs, and what never happens without you.

ctas.label: What we can and can't do

data.heading: No mystery about what happens next.

phases.title: We look
phases.body: Read-only access to the accounts and the site. We go through them and write up what we find, with the money attached.
items: You keep the findings, hired or not
A person walks you through it

phases.title: We set up
phases.body: Accounts connected, tracking verified, spend limits and approval rules set with you before anything runs.
items: Your accounts stay in your name

phases.title: We run it
phases.body: The account gets worked every day. Changes carry their evidence, a named person approves them, and you get one plain-English email a week.
items: Leads on your phone as they arrive

data.heading: What gets looked at while you're running your business.
data.body: Each check has one job and a schedule: harvest search terms, pace the budget, audit conversion tracking, flag a page that's gone stale. The software reads, researches and drafts. It writes up what it found, with the dollars at stake. It cannot apply anything.

items.title: The software proposes
items.body: Every change is written up first: what, why, and the evidence, including the money at stake. It has no ability to apply anything.

items.title: Jordan or Ted approves
items.body: A named person signs or rejects. Never their own work. Their name stays on the record next to the change.

items.title: The limits are enforced in code
items.body: Spend limits are hard limits at the point of applying. A change over the limit cannot apply, even after a human approves it.

items.title: You can stop it
items.body: One switch pauses everything on your account, instantly, without a support ticket or a phone call.

data.eyebrow: What it looks like from your side
data.heading: Email at 9:14. Fixed by 9:31.
data.body: No ticket queue, no Tuesday meeting. You ask, the software reads the live account and drafts the change, a person checks it and applies it. You get a reply, not a ticket number. An illustration of the path, not a response-time promise: turnaround depends on the change and who has to sign it.

items.body: “We're still getting calls about the $300/day ad. Can we fix it?”
Reads the live account. Finds the price extension. Drafts the removal with the evidence attached.
Checks it, approves it. Applied. You get a reply from a person.

data.heading: What we can do, what we can't, and who signs.
never: Apply a change to a live ad account without a named approver
Publish or alter a live page without a named editor
Exceed a spend limit, even with an approval behind it
Create a campaign that starts unpaused
Move, sell, or train a third-party model on your business data
Change your account ownership, billing, or who has access
always: Read your accounts and your site to find problems
Research what buyers in your market are asking
Draft a change, with its evidence and the money at stake
Flag a page that has gone stale, thin, or broken
Surface a conversion-tracking failure the moment it appears
Write up what it found, whether or not anyone acts on it
data.note: Handing anyone access to your ad accounts and your website is a real risk, and "we have human oversight" isn't an answer. This is the mechanism, in plain English.

data.heading: The answers we'd want if it were our account.

items.question: Account ownership
items.answer: Your Google, Microsoft, Meta and ChatGPT ad accounts stay in your name, with you as owner. We're granted access, and you can revoke it from your own settings without losing a day of history. Same for the domain, the phone numbers, and the content.

items.question: Data access
items.answer: We ask for read-only access to start, on the ad accounts and analytics. Write access comes only after onboarding, and only for what you've agreed to. We don't need, and don't ask for, access to billing, payroll, or customer records beyond the lead data you route to us.

items.question: How the software uses your data
items.answer: Your account data is used to do your work: inspect, research, draft. It isn't sold, shared with other clients, or used to train a third-party model. Which AI model runs a given job is an implementation detail we change when a better one ships. The approval gate doesn't change with it.

items.question: Human approvals
items.answer: Every consequential change is approved by a named person at GoLumin before it applies. Approvers don't approve their own proposals. The name, the timestamp and the original reasoning stay attached to the change.

items.question: Spend limits
items.answer: Limits are enforced in code, not by policy. A proposal over the per-change limit is blocked and shown to you as blocked. An approval doesn't override it. You set the limits during onboarding and can lower them at any time.

items.question: Audit history
items.answer: Applied changes, rejected proposals and blocked ones all stay on the record, with the evidence that was attached at the time. Clients who want to see the queue get access to their own account's history. Most prefer the weekly email.

items.question: Pause and leaving
items.answer: One switch pauses everything on your account, instantly. If you leave, the ad accounts are already yours, the content is portable, and the URLs are yours. We don't hold anything hostage as leverage on a renewal.

items.question: Retention
items.answer: We keep lead and change records for as long as you're a client and for a reasonable period afterwards so the history stays intact. Ask and we'll delete what's ours to delete. The formal version is in the privacy policy at /privacy.
